## 1. Purpose

This SOP describes field procedures for collecting soil samples
intended for molecular analysis, including DNA extraction, PCR/ddPCR,
amplicon sequencing, and metagenomics. Soil microbial communities are
sensitive to temperature, moisture, and oxygen exposure, and nucleic
acids degrade rapidly in the absence of proper preservation. The
procedures in this SOP are designed to minimize DNA and RNA degradation
from the moment of collection through transport to the laboratory,
ensuring that molecular results accurately reflect the in situ
microbial community [@knight2018; @frostegard1999].

This SOP supplements the general soil sampling procedures in
[SOP-F400](SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd) with additional precautions
specific to molecular work.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Field collection of soil and rhizosphere samples for
  DNA extraction ([SOP-L700](../lab_sops/SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd)),
  ddPCR ([SOP-L701](../lab_sops/SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd)),
  amplicon sequencing, metagenomics, and other molecular analyses
- **Does not apply to:** Soil sampling for chemical or physical
  analysis only (see [SOP-F400](SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd)); water
  eDNA sampling (see [SOP-F700](SOP-F700-edna-field-sampling.qmd));
  laboratory-side DNA extraction and processing
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve sampling design; specify target depth and
                      replication                                          |
| Trained Personnel | Collect and preserve samples per this SOP               |
| New Students      | Complete training (including contamination awareness)
                      before participating in molecular sampling           |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Biological:** Soil may contain pathogens. Wash hands thoroughly
  after handling soil. Treat all samples as potentially infectious.
- **Physical:** Repetitive strain from augering; standard field
  hazards (heat, ticks, uneven terrain).
- **Chemical:** Liquid nitrogen (if used for flash-freezing) causes
  severe cryogenic burns. Dry ice causes frostbite on direct skin
  contact. Handle with insulated gloves.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (change between samples)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or field boots
- [ ] Insulated cryogenic gloves (if using liquid nitrogen or dry ice)
- [ ] Safety glasses (if using liquid nitrogen)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). For
liquid nitrogen or dry ice burns, warm the affected area gently with
lukewarm water. Do not rub.


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Sampling Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Soil auger (bucket-type, stainless steel) | Cleaned and autoclaved or ethanol-sterilized before each sampling event |
| Stainless steel trowel or spatula     | Autoclaved or flame-sterilized           |
| Ethanol (70%) in spray bottle         | For field sterilization of tools between samples |
| Lighter or butane torch               | For flame-sterilizing metal tools        |
| DI water squeeze bottle               | For rinsing tools after ethanol sterilization |

### Sample Containers and Preservation

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Sterile 50 mL Falcon tubes or sterile Whirl-Pak bags | Pre-labeled; one per sample |
| Cooler with ice packs (4 C)           | Minimum preservation for DNA samples     |
| Dry ice (solid CO~2~)                 | For flash-freezing in the field (-78 C); preferred for RNA work |
| Insulated container for dry ice       | Styrofoam cooler or dewar                |
| LifeGuard Soil Preservation Solution (Qiagen) | Optional; stabilizes DNA and RNA at ambient temperature for up to 7 days |
| Ziplock bags (gallon size)            | For double-bagging frozen samples        |

### Field Documentation

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Field notebook (Rite in the Rain)      | For recording sample metadata            |
| Permanent marker (Sharpie)            | For labeling tubes and bags              |
| GPS unit or smartphone                | Per [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd) |
| Soil temperature probe                | Record temperature at sampling depth     |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Pre-Field Preparation

1. Autoclave or ethanol-sterilize all metal sampling tools (auger,
   trowels, spatulas). Wrap in aluminum foil after sterilization.
2. Pre-label all sample tubes or bags with: project ID, site, sample
   number, date, and depth. Use the ID scheme from
   [SOP-F008](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd).
3. If using LifeGuard solution, pre-aliquot the required volume
   (approximately 5 mL per tube for a 2--5 g soil sample) into labeled
   tubes.
4. Pack the cooler with ice packs. If using dry ice, load the
   insulated container. Ensure adequate dry ice for the expected
   number of samples and field time.
5. Include blank tubes: at least one "field blank" (an empty sterile
   tube opened and closed at the sampling site) per sampling event.

### 6.2 Sampling Procedure

1. Navigate to the sampling location and record GPS coordinates.
2. Put on a fresh pair of nitrile gloves.
3. Sterilize the auger or trowel: spray with 70% ethanol, allow to
   air-dry for 30 seconds, then optionally flame the metal surface
   with a lighter. Rinse with DI water.
4. Clear surface litter from the sampling point without disturbing the
   mineral soil surface.
5. Collect the soil sample from the target depth (typically 0--15 cm).
   Avoid including large roots and rocks.
6. Using the sterilized trowel, transfer approximately 2--5 g of soil
   (or the volume specified by the analysis protocol) directly into
   the sterile tube or bag. Minimize handling time; do not homogenize
   in a bucket as for chemical analysis, because prolonged exposure
   to air alters the microbial community.

::: {.callout-important}
### Speed Matters

For molecular samples, minimize the time between coring and
preservation. Ideally, the soil should be in the tube and on ice (or
in preservative) within 2 minutes of extraction from the ground.
Prolonged exposure to air and ambient temperature causes shifts in
microbial community composition and DNA degradation
[@frostegard1999; @knight2018].
:::

7. Immediately preserve:
   - **For DNA only:** Place the capped tube in the cooler on ice
     (4 C). Transport to the lab within 6 hours. Alternatively, bury
     the tube in dry ice for flash-freezing.
   - **For DNA and RNA:** Flash-freeze by placing the tube directly in
     dry ice or liquid nitrogen. This is critical for RNA integrity.
   - **For LifeGuard preservation:** Add LifeGuard solution to cover
     the soil, cap, invert gently 3 times, and store at ambient
     temperature (up to 7 days) or on ice for longer preservation.
8. Record in the field notebook:
   - Sample ID
   - GPS coordinates
   - Sampling depth
   - Soil temperature at sampling depth
   - Preservation method (ice, dry ice, LifeGuard)
   - Time of collection
   - Any deviations from this SOP

### 6.3 Compositing (When Required)

If the study design calls for composite molecular samples:

1. Collect subsamples from each point using sterilized tools.
2. Combine subsamples in a sterilized mixing tray or large Whirl-Pak
   bag.
3. Homogenize briefly (< 1 minute) by hand-mixing with a sterilized
   spatula.
4. Transfer an aliquot to the sterile sample tube and preserve
   immediately.
5. Be aware that compositing introduces additional handling time and
   air exposure. Note the total elapsed time from first core to
   preservation.

### 6.4 Decontamination Between Samples

1. Spray the auger, trowel, and any other tools that contacted soil
   with 70% ethanol.
2. Allow to air-dry for 30 seconds. Optionally flame-sterilize.
3. Rinse with DI water.
4. Change nitrile gloves.
5. If moving between sites, also decontaminate boots and waders per
   [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd).


## 7. Sample Transport and Storage

| Preservation Method      | Field Storage          | Transport            | Lab Storage          |
|:-------------------------|:-----------------------|:---------------------|:---------------------|
| Ice (4 C)                | Cooler with ice packs  | Same-day delivery    | Process within 24 hours or freeze at -20 C |
| Dry ice (-78 C)          | Insulated cooler       | Same-day delivery    | Transfer to -80 C freezer immediately |
| Liquid nitrogen (-196 C) | Dewar                  | Same-day delivery    | Transfer to -80 C freezer immediately |
| LifeGuard buffer         | Ambient (up to 7 days) | Standard transport   | Extract within 7 days; or freeze at -20 C |

Record sample storage location in the
[Freezer Inventory Google Sheet](<!-- LINK_PLACEHOLDER -->) and in the
lab notebook per
[SOP-L106](../lab_sops/SOP-L106-refrigerators-freezers.qmd).


## 8. Quality Control

- Include at least one field blank (empty sterile tube opened and
  closed at the site) per sampling event.
- Change gloves and sterilize tools between every sample.
- Record the time elapsed between soil extraction and preservation for
  each sample. Flag any sample with elapsed time > 5 minutes.
- Field blanks are processed through the full extraction and PCR
  workflow. Any positive amplification in a field blank invalidates
  the batch unless concentrations are below the established threshold.
- Avoid sampling immediately after rainfall when soils are saturated,
  as waterlogged conditions alter microbial activity and complicate
  extraction.

## 11. Training Record

Before collecting soil samples for molecular analysis independently,
personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F400](SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd), and
   [SOP-L700](../lab_sops/SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate sterile sampling technique (tool sterilization, glove
   changes, rapid transfer to preservative) during a supervised
   practice session
3. Successfully process a field blank with a negative extraction and
   PCR result
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
